name: Define a feature the product-truth way
summary: The way a person adds a feature to Leafcutter without writing specs by hand: they say in plain language what they want, the system classifies what the request needs and drafts the artifacts that fit — mock data, then mockups populated from it, then a flow wiring them together — and once the person reviews and approves that draft, the acceptance criteria are generated from the flow's steps. The flow becomes the reviewable source of truth the rest of the pipeline builds from.

steps.label: Say what you want
steps.human:
The person describes the feature they want in plain language — no spec format, no Gherkin, just intent.

Contract fields and examples (generated)
No JSON handoff: The person supplies natural-language intent in conversation. No JSON input DTO is defined at this human entry; downstream classifier JSON is documented on classify.

steps.label: Classify what to draft
steps.human:
The system reads the request and decides which artifacts it needs — a whole flow, mock data, mockups, or a subset — along with the component and entities involved, so it only drafts what actually fits (a full journey, a single screen, or just a dataset).

I/O boundary: This is the pt-classifier prompt output, not a labelled classifier-eval row. The pipeline remains a specification; this schema documents an existing prompt contract and does not prove orchestration is wired.

steps.label: Assemble the draft flow
steps.human:
The system assembles the steps into a draft flow, wiring each step to its screen and to the entities it reads and writes — the reviewable map of the whole journey.

I/O boundary: The draft *.flow.json is the authored contract. Examples are projections, not runnable complete flows; linked screen and AC existence is still validated against the store.

steps.label: You review & approve; ACs are generated
steps.human:
The person reviews the drafted flow (with its mock data and mockups) and approves it; acceptance criteria are then generated from the flow's steps so the flow stays the source of truth.

I/O boundary: The human approval is conversational; BA then writes parsed AC YAML and exact step.implements links. Metadata does not advance the real AC readiness or claim that generation already runs.

acceptance_scenarios.given: a person with a feature idea
acceptance_scenarios.when: they describe it in plain language
acceptance_scenarios.then: the request is captured as intent without requiring any spec or Gherkin format
it decides which of flow / mock data / mockups the request needs, with the component and entities, before anything is drafted

acceptance_scenarios.when: the system drafts the mock data
acceptance_scenarios.then: it extends the one canonical dataset for those entities rather than creating a duplicate

acceptance_scenarios.given: drafted mock data and a request that involves screens
acceptance_scenarios.then: each screen is produced and populated from that mock data

acceptance_scenarios.given: the drafted mock data and mockups
acceptance_scenarios.then: a draft flow is produced with each step wired to its screen and the entities it reads and writes
acceptance criteria are generated from the flow's steps and linked back via step.implements

Added source-bound field/type/requiredness/default metadata and explicitly illustrative JSON projections. Preserved topology, actor ownership, realization and AC status. Non-JSON artifacts and genuinely undefined proposed interfaces remain explicit.
